row.mechanism: The incomplete guard compared nesting and require to exact boolean literals, while the downstream resolver used nesting truthiness and accepted only a real require configuration. The final fix applies that structural condition before constructing the resolver.

code_evidence.summary: Claude-assisted vm2 hardening rejected only one literal option pair. Other values still built a resolver that exposed vm2 inside the sandbox, letting untrusted code create a nested NodeVM with access to host modules.

steps.title: AI change
steps.detail: The Claude-coauthored guard blocked only { nesting: true, require: false }.

steps.title: Security fix
steps.detail: The final patch rejects every nesting/require shape that would create a vm2-only resolver.

steps.title: AI change
steps.detail: The Claude-generated release made safeDialContext the dial boundary but shipped an incomplete IPv6 denylist.

steps.title: Security fix
steps.detail: The final patch adds the four omitted IPv6 prefixes and checks them before dialing.

candidate_hunks.annotation: The released Claude-assisted hardening imports net so namespace verification can resolve and classify addresses before dialing.
The default HTTP fetcher is routed through safeDialContext, making its address classifier the security boundary for attacker-controlled publisher domains.

safeDialContext blocks the usual private, loopback, link-local, multicast, unspecified, and CGNAT ranges, but its list omits 6to4, both NAT64 prefixes, and deprecated site-local IPv6. Routed IPv6 wrappers can therefore carry an internal IPv4 destination through this allow decision.

fix_hunks.annotation: The direct fix adds fail-fast CIDR parsing and explicitly rejects 2002::/16, 64:ff9b::/96, 64:ff9b:1::/48, and fec0::/10 before dialing. Iterating those prefixes closes each IPv6 translation or site-local route omitted by the original classifier.
